name: expectation error
description: Moderate negativity coming from a perception that an important expectation was found to be incorrect. It's a brief sadness about being wrong, separate from the implications of being wrong.
perceptions: In order to live in the world, I need to understand it.
This perception conflicting with my expectation suggests that I may not understand this part correctly.
I had prepared myself for a particular outcome that seemed to be important.
results: An expectation failing is just the first spark of what may be an avalanche of sensations. If you were wrong about expecting something bad happened, you may not care much about being wrong. If you were wrong about something good happening, you may be doubly sad.
examples: Being wrong about thinking they were going to throw you a surprise party.
The voting didn't go the way you'd predicted.

variations.name: prediction error
variations.description: A twinge of negativity coming from a perception that a low-impact prediction (or assumption) was found to be incorrect. It's a brief mild sadness about being wrong, separate from the implications of being wrong.
perceptions: In order to live in the world, I need to understand it.
This perception conflicting with my prediction suggests that I may not understand this part correctly.
It's a bummer I was wrong, but it doesn't affect me all that much.
results: A prediction failing is the first spark of what may be many sensations. If you were wrong about predicting something bad, you may not care much about being wrong. If you were wrong about a prediction of something good happening, you may be doubly dissatisfied.
examples: Failing the Wordle after thinking you would solve it.
The sports team didn't win as predicted.

variations.name: guess error
variations.description: A mild dissatisfaction coming from a perception that a low-impact prediction was found to be incorrect.
perceptions: In order to live in the world, I need to understand it.
This perception conflicting with my guess suggests that I may not understand this part correctly.
results: A failed guess is perceived as no big deal. It means future guesses may be more accurate.
examples: You didn't guess the lottery number right.

variations.name: core assumption error
variations.description: A tidal wave of negativity coming from a perception that a high-impact assumption or belief was found to be incorrect.
perceptions: In order to live in the world, I need to understand it.
This perception conflicting with my prediction suggests that I may not understand this part correctly.
It's a complete disaster or triumph for a core identity that I was wrong.
It will have a major effect on me.
results: A failed assumption or belief is the first spark of what may be an avalanche sensations. If you were wrong about assuming something bad, you may be happy about being wrong. If you were wrong about a prediction of something good happening, you may experience grief.
examples: You had assumed your dad's politics were very different than your own.
You're forced to change a belief about the honor of your country.

comparisons.description: These are all similar, differing in how much confidence you had in the pattern and the impact to your life. You're most invested in 'core assumptions', so finding one that's wrong can be a shock, normally in negative way. You're somewhat less invested in 'expectations', so being wrong about them has a notable impact. You're not very invested in 'predictions' so a 'prediction error' doesn't matter so much in the big picture. Finally, you're not emotionally invested in a 'guess' at all, so after a tiny disappointment about being wrong, you've already moved on.

commentaries.quote: The proactive approach to a mistake is to acknowledge it instantly, correct and learn from it.
People need to be wrong as fast as they can.
Allow yourself to go and do it wrong. Don’t expect to always get it right. It will prevent you from doing anything.
We all can be wrong, some more often than others.
The unconscious mind will often warp perceptual reality to avoid being faced with the realization that a core belief is wrong.
